consoleSteps.note: Identity check: sts:GetCallerIdentity Lambda operations: lambda:CreateFunction, lambda:InvokeFunction, lambda:GetFunction, lambda:UpdateFunctionCode, lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration, lambda:DeleteFunction IAM setup: iam:CreateRole, iam:PassRole

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
Use the Region eu-west-2 (Europe London) or your preferred standard Region for these labs.
Confirm that your console theme is set to dark or standard preference.
In the search bar at the top, type Lambda and select it from the services list.
Choose Create function.
Keep the default selection: Author from scratch.
For Function name, enter saa-test-compute.
For Runtime, choose the latest stable version of Python 3.11.
Keep Architecture set to x86_64.
Expand the Change default execution role section.
Select Create a new role with basic Lambda permissions.
Choose Create function at the bottom of the page.

consoleSteps.title: Modify and deploy the function code

instructions.text: Locate the Code source file tree pane inside the function overview tab.
Double-click the main handler file (e.g., lambda_function.py) to open it.
Replace the default return payload message with: 'Invocations running at zero cost under Free Tier'.
Click the Deploy button above the file tree to save and publish your modifications.

consoleSteps.note: Always click Deploy to make your code changes active. Saving the file is not enough.

instructions.text: Click the Test tab next to the Code panel.
For Event action, keep Create new event selected.
For Event name, enter mockClickstreamEvent.
For Template, keep hello-world selected.
Leave the default dummy JSON payload intact.
Choose Save at the top right of the Test configuration panel.

consoleSteps.title: Execute and verify the mock invocation

instructions.text: With your newly created mockClickstreamEvent selected, click the orange Test button.
Wait for the execution to complete and locate the Execution result panel.
Expand the result details dropdown to view logs and execution metrics.
Verify that the status is Succeeded and the response body displays your custom string.
Analyze the billing metrics, noting the Duration, Billed Duration, Memory Size (128 MB), and Max Memory Used.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down resources

instructions.text: Go back to the top of your function's configuration page.
Choose Actions → Delete function.
Type delete to confirm deletion.
Choose Delete.
Open the IAM Console, navigate to Roles, and delete the execution role that Lambda created for your function.

consoleSteps.warning: Do not delete active company roles. Verify the role name matches the lambda-basic-execution role generated during function creation.

cliSteps.title: Check your AWS identity
cliSteps.note: Expected: you see your AWS account ID and ARN.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Expected: you see your AWS account ID and ARN.

cliSteps.title: Create Lambda function

commands.text: aws lambda create-function --function-name saa-test-compute --runtime python3.11 --role <YOUR_ROLE_ARN> --handler lambda_function.lambda_handler --zip-file fileb://function.zip

cliSteps.note: Replace with the role ARN from Step 1. Ensure function.zip contains your code.

cliSteps.title: Invoke the function
cliSteps.note: Verify output.json contains 'Invocations running at zero cost under Free Tier'.

cliSteps.title: Clean up resources

commands.text:
aws lambda delete-function --function-name saa-test-compute
aws iam detach-role-policy --role-name lambda-basic-execution --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
aws iam delete-role --role-name lambda-basic-execution

cliSteps.warning: Destructive Command Warning: This command permanently deletes serverless functions, APIs, state machines, rules, queues, or topics.

verification.text: AWS Lambda configuration verified in AWS Lambda.

Delete the AWS Lambda function and associated CloudWatch Log Group.

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
Use the Region eu-west-2 (Europe London) or your preferred standard Region for these labs.
Confirm that your console theme is set to dark or standard preference.
Open the AWS Lambda console.
Select your saa-test-compute function.
Select the Configuration tab below the function header.
Choose Concurrency from the left-hand configuration sidebar.
Under the Concurrency configuration card, locate Reserved concurrency.
Click the Edit button.
Select the Reserve concurrency option.
Input an explicit value of 5.
Note that this reserve decreases the remaining unreserved concurrency pool for other regional functions.
Click Save to apply the changes.
Under the Provisioned concurrency section, click Add configuration.
Choose Alias or Version as the qualifier (e.g., Version 1).
Enter a provisioned concurrency value of 2.
Carefully read the pricing prompt showing that Provisioned Concurrency starts charging hourly fees immediately.
Choose Cancel to abort and protect your $0 Free Tier sandbox perimeter.
Go back to the Reserved concurrency section and click Edit.
Select Use unreserved account concurrency.
Click Save to release the reserved execution threads.

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
Use the Region eu-west-2 (Europe London) or your preferred standard Region for these labs.
Confirm that your console theme is set to dark or standard preference.
Open the Amazon EventBridge console.
Select Buses → Rules and click Create rule.
For Name, enter catch-ec2-state-adjustments.
Keep Event bus set to default.
Select Rule with an event pattern and click Next.

consoleSteps.title: Define EC2 State Change event pattern

instructions.text: Under Event source, select AWS services.
In the Event pattern dropdowns, choose EC2 as the AWS service.
Choose EC2 Instance State-change Notification as the Event type.
Click Next.
On the Select target page, choose AWS service.
Select Lambda function from the target type dropdown.
Choose your saa-test-compute function.
Click Next through tags and click Create rule.
Select the rule catch-ec2-state-adjustments.
Click Delete and confirm.

cliSteps.title: Check your AWS identity
cliSteps.note: Expected: you see your AWS account ID and ARN.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Expected: you see your AWS account ID and ARN.

cliSteps.title: Create EventBridge infrastructure state monitoring rule

commands.text: aws events put-rule --name catch-ec2-state-adjustments --event-pattern '{"source":["aws.ec2"],"detail-type":["EC2 Instance State-change Notification"]}'

cliSteps.title: Clean up EventBridge rule and target

commands.text: aws events remove-targets --rule catch-ec2-state-adjustments --ids "1" && aws events delete-rule --name catch-ec2-state-adjustments

cliSteps.warning: Destructive Command Warning: This command permanently deletes serverless functions, APIs, state machines, rules, queues, or topics.

cleanup.text: Remove all rule targets and delete the EventBridge rule.
Delete custom event buses, schedules, or DLQs if created for the lab.

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.

Type a dummy message string into the message body input area.

Select the checkbox for order-ingestion-buffer.
Click Delete and confirm deletion.

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
Use the Region eu-west-2 (Europe London) or your preferred standard Region for these labs.
Confirm that your console theme is set to dark or standard preference.
Open the Amazon SQS console and click Create queue.
Select FIFO as the queue type.
For Name, enter order-pipeline.fifo (note that SQS enforces the .fifo suffix).
Locate the Content-based deduplication toggle switch.
Turn it on to auto-hash message payloads using SHA-256 for 5-minute deduplication windows.
Click Create queue.
Review the queue details page, noting the specific Message Group ID and Message Deduplication ID constraints required for FIFO delivery.
Select order-pipeline.fifo from the SQS queue list.
Click Delete, type delete, and confirm.

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
Use the Region eu-west-2 (Europe London) or your preferred standard Region for these labs.
Confirm that your console theme is set to dark or standard preference.
Open S3 console and click Create bucket.
Name the bucket with a unique prefix (e.g. saa-payload-vault-[account-id]).
Click Create bucket.
Open the SQS console and choose your order-ingestion-buffer queue.
Review the maximum message size parameter, noting it is hard-capped at 256 KB.
To send payloads larger than 256 KB, the client library uploads the raw payload to S3 first.
The client library then sends an SQS message containing only the S3 bucket name and key path pointer.
The receiver client automatically pulls the S3 pointer, retrieves the payload from S3, and processes it.
Delete the S3 payload bucket and standard queue.

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.

Select Standard type.
Name the topic broadcast-events.

Inside the broadcast-events topic dashboard, click Create subscription.
For Protocol, select Amazon SQS.
In the Endpoint field, paste the ARN of your SQS Standard queue from Task 5.
Expand the Subscription filter policy accordion section.
Enable the policy.
Enter the JSON matching policy: {"transaction_type": ["premium"]}.
Click Create subscription.
Select the subscription in the list and click Delete.
Select the topic broadcast-events and click Delete.
